transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up at work and that everyone can see how worthless I am, like it’s all being recorded as proof. It’s gotten so bad that my manager actually sent me home mid-shift, and I just feel completely overwhelmed by it all.
Did these feelings of being worthless and down start first, or did you begin noticing the feeling of being recorded before your mood changed?

The heavy, dark feeling and feeling worthless definitely started first. It was only after I sank into this deep depression that I began feeling like everything was being recorded against me. On the rare days when my mood lifts even just a little, those thoughts seem to fade into the background too.
Have you ever had periods in your life lasting at least a few days where you felt the exact opposite—extremely energetic, needing very little sleep, or feeling on top of the world?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. My mood has always been the complete opposite, mostly just feeling really heavy, down, and drained. I've never had periods where I felt on top of the world or had that kind of high energy.
Have you ever experienced a period of deep depression like this before in your life, or is this the very first time you've felt this way?

I’ve never felt anything like this before in my life; this is definitely the first time I've experienced such a deep, overwhelming depression. It's completely different from any normal sadness I've ever felt, and it just feels impossible to shake.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-time severe depressive episode characterized by a persistent heavy, dark mood, lack of energy, and intense feelings of worthlessness. This is accompanied by mood-congruent psychotic symptoms (delusions of being recorded as proof of their worthlessness and failure at work). The depressive symptoms preceded the psychotic symptoms, and the psychotic thoughts fade when the depression lifts slightly. There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, confirming a single episode of severe depression with psychotic symptoms (F32.3).
